title: Java & Object-Oriented Programming
description: Test your mastery of Java 21, JVM internals, OOP principles, multi-threading, and stream processing.

questions.text: Which of the following is true regarding Java virtual threads introduced in Java 21 (Project Loom)?
options: They map 1:1 directly to operating system kernel threads
They are lightweight threads managed by the JVM that drastically reduce memory overhead for concurrent tasks
They replace the need for garbage collection in Java
They can only run on single-core CPU architectures
questions.explanation: Virtual threads are lightweight threads managed by the Java Virtual Machine rather than the underlying OS, allowing applications to handle millions of concurrent connections with minimal memory and context switching overhead.

questions.text: Which of these concepts are core pillars of Object-Oriented Programming in Java?
questions.explanation: The four fundamental pillars of OOP are Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, and Polymorphism. Pipelining is a hardware / stream concept.

questions.text: Java's String class is immutable. Once created, a String object's internal character sequence cannot be changed.
questions.explanation: Strings in Java are immutable for security, thread safety, caching, and string pool optimization. Modifications create a new String instance.

questions.text: What happens when an exception is thrown inside a try block with an attached finally block?
options: The finally block is skipped if an exception occurs
The finally block always executes (unless System.exit() or JVM crash occurs)
The finally block only executes if the exception is caught
The program halts before reaching finally
questions.explanation: The finally block is guaranteed to execute whether an exception is caught or uncaught, making it ideal for cleaning up resources like file streams or database connections.

questions.text: Which collection implementation in Java allows key-value pairs with null keys and is not synchronized by default?
questions.explanation: HashMap allows one null key and multiple null values and is unsynchronized. Hashtable and ConcurrentHashMap do not allow null keys.

title: Data Structures & Algorithms in Java
description: Challenge yourself with algorithmic complexity, binary search trees, dynamic programming, and graphs.

questions.text: What is the average time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL or Red-Black Tree)?
questions.explanation: Because a balanced BST halves the search space at every step, the height of the tree is bounded by O(log n), resulting in O(log n) average and worst-case search complexity.

questions.text: Which data structure uses the LIFO (Last In First Out) principle?
questions.explanation: A Stack operates on LIFO (Last In First Out) principle, commonly used for function call call-stacks, undo operations, and expression evaluation.

questions.text: Which of the following sorting algorithms have a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n)?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort and Heap Sort guarantee O(n log n) even in the worst case. Standard QuickSort degrades to O(n^2) with poor pivot selection.

questions.text: Breadth-First Search (BFS) on a graph uses a FIFO Queue to visit neighbors level by level.
questions.explanation: BFS systematically traverses nodes level by level using a FIFO Queue, finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs.

title: Firebase & Cloud Firestore Mastery
description: Demonstrate your understanding of Google Firebase, Firestore NoSQL architecture, Security Rules, and Realtime sync.

questions.text: How does Cloud Firestore organize data compared to the traditional Firebase Realtime Database?
options: Firestore uses a single giant JSON tree, whereas Realtime DB uses relational tables
Firestore stores data in documents grouped inside collections with rich querying capabilities
Firestore only allows binary blobs up to 10MB
Firestore requires SQL schema migrations for every table
questions.explanation: Cloud Firestore is a flexible NoSQL document database that organizes data into documents and collections, supporting shallow queries, subcollections, and automatic scaling.

questions.text: Which authentication providers are supported out-of-the-box by Firebase Authentication?
questions.explanation: Firebase Authentication supports Email/Password, phone numbers, anonymous logins, and popular federated identity providers such as Google, GitHub, Facebook, Twitter, Apple, and Microsoft.

questions.text: In Cloud Firestore, querying a collection automatically downloads all data stored in its subcollections as well.
questions.explanation: Firestore queries are shallow by design! Querying a collection retrieves only documents within that collection; subcollections are not fetched unless queried explicitly.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of Firebase Security Rules?
options: To format JSON data before printing in the terminal
To control user access, authenticate requests, and validate data schema on Firestore and Storage directly from client SDKs
To compile Java bytecode on the server
To encrypt your local hard drive
questions.explanation: Firebase Security Rules allow developers to specify granular authorization policies, ensuring users only read or write documents they are permitted to access directly from web or mobile clients.

title: Modern Web Architecture & REST APIs
description: Essential principles of client-server architecture, HTTP protocols, RESTful guidelines, and JSON web tokens.

questions.text: Which HTTP status code signifies that a resource was successfully created on the server?
questions.explanation: HTTP 201 Created indicates that the request has succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource, typically returned from POST requests.

questions.text: Which HTTP methods are typically considered idempotent in REST API design?
questions.explanation: An idempotent HTTP method can be called multiple times with the same result as calling it once. GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent; POST is not idempotent.

questions.text: A JSON Web Token (JWT) is composed of Header, Payload, and Signature separated by dots.
questions.explanation: JWT structure is 'header.payload.signature', encoded in Base64URL and cryptographically verifiable.
